scenes.title: 1970 Columbia / NYU Neurobiology Bench: Giant Aplysia Porcelain Model, Dual Microelectrodes & '1,300 -> 2,600 Doubled Synapses' Chart
scenes.era: 1970, NYU / Columbia University Neurobiology Laboratory, New York

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1970 New York neurobiology laboratory featuring a crystal-clear seawater glass dish holding an **articulated matte-white porcelain Aplysia sea-hare sculpture**, flanked by twin precision micromanipulator arms lowering glass microelectrodes onto a large educational 2-neuron ('Sensory -> Motor') circuit diagram, beside a crisp chart comparing **Short-Term (1,300 Terminals) vs Long-Term Spaced Training (2,600 Terminals — Doubled!)**.

positions.who: Eric Kandel (mannequin in 1970 crisp white lab coat, collared shirt, and signature red bow tie)
positions.where: adjusting the gentle water-jet pipette beside the seawater dish while pointing from the oscilloscope synaptic potential jump to the '1,300 -> 2,600 Synaptic Terminals' structural growth plaque

positions.who: Vincent Castellucci / Irving Kupfermann (mannequin in 1970 rolled-sleeve Oxford shirt under lab coat)
positions.where: recording paired presynaptic and postsynaptic trace amplitudes in the 1970 Science laboratory notebook

props.name: articulated matte-white porcelain Aplysia sea-hare sculpture in clear glass dish & gentle water-jet pipette
props.period_detail: clean museum-grade porcelain marine model showing siphon-to-gill reflex geometry

props.name: dual micromanipulator probes & twin-trace EPSP oscilloscope
props.period_detail: records the exact single synapse between siphon sensory cell and gill motor cell

props.name: '850 (Habituated) | 1,300 (Baseline) | 2,600 (Long-Term Spaced)' terminal-tree plaque
props.period_detail: visualizes physical pruning and doubling of synaptic branches
props.physical_behavior: proves long-term memory is new anatomy

actions.verb_sequence: applies a gentle spaced water-jet training sequence -> points as the postsynaptic wave doubles on the oscilloscope AND switches to the structural plaque showing 1,300 terminals branching out into 2,600 terminals

reactions.reaction: logs intact short-term trace vs protein-dependent long-term terminal doubling
beams with his trademark bow-tie warmth as one simple synapse unlocks memory's molecular alphabet

scenes.wardrobe: 1970 academic laboratory attire: crisp white lab coat, blue Oxford button-down, signature bow tie.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key New York laboratory daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: With 20,000 giant naked-eye neurons, a humble sea snail proved long-term memories physically double the connections between brain cells.

key_visual.description: a 1970 neurobiology bench where a bow-tied researcher in a lab coat stands beside a clear dish holding a matte-white porcelain Aplysia sculpture, micromanipulators, an oscilloscope, and a 1300-to-2600 synaptic terminal chart

scenes.title: Why Cramming Fails & Spaced Sessions Flip CREB On
scenes.era: 1990, Columbia Center for Neurobiology and Behavior

layout.description: Bright teaching table contrasting '4 Crammed Trials (Local cAMP Only)' against '4 Spaced Trials (Nuclear CREB-1 -> New Terminals)'.

positions.where: showing why spaced gaps let PKA reach the cell nucleus to lift the CREB-2 brake and build permanent hardware

props.name: Crammed Chemical vs Spaced Structural comparison board
props.period_detail: explains Ebbinghaus's 1885 spacing law at the gene level

actions.verb_sequence: flips the CREB-1 switch ON strictly on the spaced-training track

reactions.reaction: vow never to rely on last-minute cramming again

scenes.recognition_hook: Cramming only turns up temporary chemical volume at the tip — spaced practice sends a messenger into the cell nucleus to build twice as many wires.

scenes.title: Conserved Across 500 Million Years: Matte-White Porcelain Sea-Slug to Mouse to Human

layout.description: Warm sunlit lecture hall displaying matte-white porcelain Aplysia sea-slug, porcelain fruit-fly, and mammalian hippocampus models sharing the identical cAMP -> PKA -> CREB pathway.

positions.where: delivering his 2000 Nobel Lecture pointing across the conserved evolutionary memory alphabet

props.name: 3-species conserved CREB memory plaque
props.period_detail: vindicates Kandel's bold 1962 bet on a simple marine organism

actions.verb_sequence: gestures across all three species sharing one molecular memory switch

scenes.wardrobe: Tailored dark suit and bow tie.
scenes.recognition_hook: Evolution didn't reinvent memory for humans — it kept the exact molecular CREB switch perfected half a billion years ago in the sea.

layout.description: Sunlit desk with four spaced 25-minute study blocks followed by restful sleep.

props.name: 4-day spaced schedule card
props.period_detail: aligns daily study habits with CREB transcription timing

actions.verb_sequence: checks off Session 3 of 4 and closes book on time for full sleep

scenes.recognition_hook: You walk out of every spaced study session with a slightly different anatomical brain than the one you walked in with.
